punchline: Tracy says starting and stopping a task has been estimated to stretch it by as much as 500 percent, though he cites no source.
thirty_sec: Brian Tracy's last rule is to pick your most important task and stay on it until it is done, telling yourself 'back to work' whenever you drift. His reason is the restart: each time you return you have to find your place and rebuild your rhythm. His fix is thirty, sixty or ninety minute blocks with the phone off. His example is a salesperson who spends one hour, 10 to 11 AM, only phoning prospects.
